sources.citation: CDC WONDER Drug Overdose Mortality Data

metadata.description: 10-year risk of death from drug overdose, including opioids, stimulants, and other substances

curves.source: Derived from the unstratified NCHS curve using the male:female drug-overdose mortality ratio ~2.4 (NCHS Data Briefs 522/549: age-adjusted 2022-2024 male 45.6/44.3/32.2 vs female 19.4/18.3/14.1 per 100k; ratio stable across ages 15-74 per Butelman et al. 2023, doi:10.1101/2023.01.20.23284833)
curves.notes: male = 1.41x combined, female = 0.59x combined (equal population shares)

riskFactors.name: Opioid Daily Dose (MME)
riskFactors.citation: Bohnert ASB, Valenstein M, Bair MJ, et al. Association Between Opioid Prescribing Patterns and Opioid Overdose-Related Deaths. JAMA. 2011;305(13):1315-1321; CDC Guideline for Prescribing Opioids for Chronic Pain. MMWR Recomm Rep. 2016;65(1)
riskFactors.notes: VA cohort fatal-overdose HRs vs 1-20 MME/day reference: 20-49 -> 1.9, 50-99 -> 4.6, >=100 -> 7.2; plateau above 100 (no data). Reference category is low-dose users, not non-users.

riskFactors.name: Prescribed Benzodiazepines

mapping.notes: Benzos + opioids = very high risk combination

riskFactors.citation: Park TW, Saitz R, Ganoczy D, Ilgen MA, Bohnert ASB. Benzodiazepine prescribing patterns and deaths from drug overdose among US veterans receiving opioid analgesics: case-cohort study. BMJ. 2015;350:h2698
riskFactors.notes: Current benzodiazepine prescription among opioid recipients: overdose-death aHR 3.86 (3.49-4.26); concurrent-use estimate elsewhere 2.11 (1.70-2.62). 3.0 is a conservative middle that also fires without opioid co-prescription.

riskFactors.name: Substance Abuse History
riskFactors.notes: Polysubstance use OR~4.0 for overdose mortality

mapping.notes: History of substance abuse is strongest predictor

riskFactors.name: Prior Overdose

mapping.notes: Prior overdose dramatically increases future risk

riskFactors.citation: Olfson M, Crystal S, Wall M, Wang S, Liu SM, Blanco C. Causes of Death After Nonfatal Opioid Overdose. JAMA Psychiatry. 2018;75(8):820-827
riskFactors.notes: Comparator-dependent: within people who inject drugs, recent nonfatal overdose aHR 1.95 (1.17-3.27); vs the GENERAL population, first-year all-cause SMR after nonfatal opioid overdose is 24.2 (drug-related SMR 132). HR 10 is a deliberately conservative population-baseline multiplier.

riskFactors.name: Depression Diagnosis
riskFactors.citation: Weiner SG, El Ibrahimi S, Hendricks MA, et al. Factors Associated With Opioid Overdose After an Initial Opioid Prescription. JAMA Netw Open. 2022;5(1):e2145691
riskFactors.notes: Depression aHR 1.26 (1.03-1.55) for opioid overdose; repeated-overdose cohort aHR 1.44 (1.17-1.78). The larger effects in this literature belong to substance use disorder (aHR 2.74), modeled separately.

riskFactors.name: Alcohol Consumption

mapping.notes: Alcohol mixed with substances increases overdose risk

riskFactors.citation: Substance use and use disorders among Veterans on long-term opioid therapy (VHA cohort 2014-2019)
riskFactors.notes: Alcohol use disorder: fatal-overdose HR 1.43 (1.10-1.86) among long-term opioid therapy patients; exp(0.03x) reaches 1.43 at ~12 drinks/week. Capped at ~23 drinks/week (HR ~2.0) — nothing beyond the AUD-level effect is evidenced.
